kyoto.name: Kyoto
kyoto.description: Shrines, temples and gardens in a city that preserves centuries of Japanese tradition.
kyoto.imageAlt: Path of red torii gates at the Fushimi Inari shrine in Kyoto
kyoto.longDescription: The imperial capital of Japan for over a thousand years, Kyoto is home to many temples and shrines, traditional gardens and historic districts such as Gion. The path of torii gates at Fushimi Inari shrine is one of the city's best-known scenes.

paris.name: Paris
paris.description: Museums, cafés and elegant avenues along the Seine, from art to fashion and food.
paris.longDescription: The capital of France, Paris brings together museums such as the Louvre, the Eiffel Tower, the Seine and neighborhoods full of cafés and bookshops. It is a classic destination for lovers of art, architecture and good food.

lisbon.name: Lisbon
lisbon.description: Hills, viewpoints and vintage trams above the Tagus, with a lively food scene.
lisbon.imageAlt: View from the Portas do Sol viewpoint in Lisbon
lisbon.longDescription: The capital of Portugal, Lisbon spreads across hills beside the Tagus river. Districts such as Alfama and Bairro Alto, its viewpoints and yellow trams give the city a rhythm of its own, along with traditional Portuguese cooking.

bali.name: Bali
bali.description: Terraced rice fields, temples and beaches on a tropical island of lush nature.
bali.longDescription: An island of Indonesia known for its rice terraces, Hindu temples and beaches. The interior around Ubud is a center for art and crafts, while the coast offers beaches for different travel styles.

newyork.name: New York
newyork.description: Skyscrapers, parks, museums and a food scene that gathers the world in one city.
newyork.imageAlt: Midtown Manhattan skyline at night in New York
newyork.longDescription: The most populous city in the United States brings together Manhattan, Central Park, museums such as the Metropolitan and a huge variety of cuisines. Every borough has its own personality, from Brooklyn to Queens.

rome.longDescription: The capital of Italy, Rome preserves ancient ruins such as the Colosseum and the Roman Forum, alongside baroque squares and the nearby Vatican. Roman cooking, simple and flavorful, is part of the experience.
rome.name: Rome
rome.description: Ancient ruins, baroque squares and a cuisine that makes the table part of the story.

capetown.longDescription: A South African city between Table Mountain and the ocean, with beaches, nearby vineyards and the Cape Peninsula. It combines striking nature, history and a diverse food scene.
capetown.name: Cape Town
capetown.description: Between Table Mountain and the ocean, a city of striking landscapes and good food.
capetown.imageAlt: Table Mountain seen from Bloubergstrand, in Cape Town

rio.longDescription: A Brazilian city between mountains and sea, with beaches such as Copacabana and Ipanema, Sugarloaf Mountain and Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado. Nature and city life meet within a few kilometers.
rio.name: Rio de Janeiro
rio.description: Mountains, beaches and Carioca energy in one of the world's most iconic urban landscapes.
rio.imageAlt: Sugarloaf Mountain seen from Christ the Redeemer, in Rio de Janeiro

vancouver.longDescription: A Canadian city between the Pacific Ocean and the mountains, with Stanley Park, a waterfront and access to trails and skiing nearby. It blends urban life and nature.
vancouver.name: Vancouver
vancouver.description: Ocean, mountains and city parks within minutes of each other.

istanbul.longDescription: A city that spans two continents, Europe and Asia, divided by the Bosphorus strait. Monuments such as Hagia Sophia, bazaars and Turkish cuisine reflect centuries of history.
istanbul.name: Istanbul
istanbul.description: A city between two continents, with ancient monuments, bazaars and Turkish flavors.

seoul.name: Seoul
seoul.description: Joseon-dynasty palaces, cafés, design and a vibrant food scene between mountains and the Han River.
seoul.longDescription: South Korea's capital, where Joseon-dynasty palaces such as Gyeongbokgung sit alongside design districts, cafés and street markets. The Han River and the surrounding mountains put hiking trails minutes from the center, and the table ranges from Korean barbecue to tteokbokki.

bangkok.name: Bangkok
bangkok.description: Golden temples, canals and street food celebrated worldwide, in a capital that never slows down.
bangkok.longDescription: Thailand's capital on the Chao Phraya River, where temples such as Wat Arun and Wat Pho share the skyline with skyscrapers. Boats cross the canals, markets run from dawn until late at night, and street food is central to the experience.
bangkok.imageAlt: Wat Arun, the Temple of Dawn, in Bangkok

singapore.name: Singapore
singapore.description: A city-state of skyscrapers, futuristic gardens and food centers that bring many cultures to one table.
singapore.longDescription: A city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, where Marina Bay, Gardens by the Bay and neighborhoods such as Chinatown and Little India sit within a few kilometers of each other. Its hawker centers, recognized by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage, serve Chinese, Malay and Indian dishes at modest prices.
singapore.imageAlt: Marina Bay and the Singapore skyline at dusk

mumbai.name: Mumbai
mumbai.description: Colonial architecture, Bollywood cinema and the Arabian Sea in a city of contrasts.
mumbai.longDescription: One of India's largest cities, on the Arabian Sea, where the Gateway of India and Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, a Victorian Gothic UNESCO World Heritage site, tell its colonial story. The Marine Drive seafront, bustling markets and street food such as vada pav complete the picture of a city in constant motion.
mumbai.imageAlt: The Gateway of India in Mumbai

hanoi.name: Hanoi
hanoi.description: A lake, Old Quarter alleys and cafés in a capital that blends tradition, French heritage and bold flavors.
hanoi.longDescription: Vietnam's capital, organized around Hoan Kiem Lake and the Old Quarter, whose narrow streets still carry the names of traditional trades. French-influenced avenues and buildings sit beside temples, and the table offers phở, bún chả and egg coffee.

osaka.name: Osaka
osaka.description: A castle, the Dotonbori district and a reputation as Japan's food capital.
osaka.longDescription: One of Japan's largest cities, long known as "the nation's kitchen". Osaka Castle recalls its past power, while neon-lit Dotonbori is packed with takoyaki and okonomiyaki stalls. Kyoto and Nara are under an hour away by train.

marrakech.name: Marrakech
marrakech.description: An ochre-walled medina, fragrant souks and Jemaa el-Fna square, in the shadow of the Atlas.
marrakech.longDescription: An imperial city at the foot of the Atlas Mountains, with a walled, UNESCO-listed medina of alleys, souks and hidden gardens. At dusk Jemaa el-Fna square fills with musicians, storytellers and food stalls, while the minaret of the Koutoubia dominates the skyline.

cairo.name: Cairo
cairo.description: The Giza pyramids, pharaonic museums and a maze of bazaars on the Nile.
cairo.longDescription: Egypt's capital on the Nile, a few kilometers from the Pyramids of Giza, the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing. Islamic Cairo holds mosques and the Khan el-Khalili bazaar, and the city layers centuries of history into its busy streets.
cairo.imageAlt: The Pyramids of Giza near Cairo

nairobi.name: Nairobi
nairobi.description: A capital with a savanna national park at its edge and the starting point for safaris.
nairobi.longDescription: Kenya's capital and gateway to safaris is one of the few capitals in the world with a national park within its limits: lions, giraffes and rhinos live against a backdrop of skyscrapers. The city also has elephant and giraffe sanctuaries, museums and a growing café and music scene.

toronto.name: Toronto
toronto.description: The CN Tower, neighborhoods from around the world and the Lake Ontario islands in a multicultural metropolis.
toronto.longDescription: Canada's largest city, on the shore of Lake Ontario, famous for the CN Tower and a population drawn from all over the world. Neighborhoods such as Kensington Market, Chinatown and the Distillery District show that diversity, and the Toronto Islands offer beaches and skyline views a short ferry ride away.

mexicocity.name: Mexico City
mexicocity.description: Museums, murals, markets and a UNESCO-recognized cuisine in a capital at 2,240 meters.
mexicocity.longDescription: Mexico's capital, built on the ancient Aztec city of Tenochtitlan, brings together the Zócalo, the Palacio de Bellas Artes and the National Museum of Anthropology. Diego Rivera's murals, Frida Kahlo's Blue House in Coyoacán and markets such as La Merced show the strength of local culture, from art to the dinner table.
mexicocity.imageAlt: Palacio de Bellas Artes in Mexico City

buenosaires.name: Buenos Aires
buenosaires.description: Tango, grand bookshops, historic cafés and broad avenues in a capital with a European air.
buenosaires.longDescription: Argentina's capital, where Avenida 9 de Julio, one of the widest avenues in the world, is marked by the Obelisco. Neighborhoods such as San Telmo, with its antiques market and milongas, and colorful La Boca keep tango alive, while historic cafés and bookshops such as El Ateneo Grand Splendid, set in a former theater, round out the itinerary.
buenosaires.imageAlt: Avenida 9 de Julio and the Obelisco in Buenos Aires

santiago.name: Santiago
santiago.description: A capital ringed by the Andes, with nearby vineyards and a growing food scene.
santiago.longDescription: Chile's capital sits in a valley surrounded by the Andes, whose snow-capped peaks frame the skyline on clear days. Santa Lucía and San Cristóbal hills offer views and trails inside the city, and wineries of the Maipo Valley are less than an hour from the center.

cusco.name: Cusco
cusco.description: The former Inca capital, with stone streets, colonial squares and the gateway to Machu Picchu.
cusco.longDescription: At about 3,400 meters in the Peruvian Andes, Cusco was the capital of the Inca Empire and blends Inca walls with colonial churches, such as the Church of the Society of Jesus on the Plaza de Armas. It is the starting point for the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu, and its cuisine draws on Andean potatoes, corn and quinoa.

prague.name: Prague
prague.description: Bridges, towers and red roofs in one of Europe's best-preserved medieval capitals.
prague.longDescription: The capital of the Czech Republic, cut by the Vltava River, with Prague Castle crowning the hill and Charles Bridge linking the Old Town to Malá Strana. The UNESCO-listed historic center has the astronomical clock and traditional breweries, and goulash with knedlíky is a typical dish.

amsterdam.name: Amsterdam
amsterdam.description: Seventeenth-century canals, narrow houses, art museums and a city built for bikes.
amsterdam.longDescription: The capital of the Netherlands, where the UNESCO-listed seventeenth-century canal ring is lined with tall, narrow houses. The Rijksmuseum and the Van Gogh Museum hold works by Dutch masters, the bicycle is the main way to get around, and markets sell stroopwafels and herring.

vienna.name: Vienna
vienna.description: Imperial palaces, opera and traditional cafés in the capital of classical music.
vienna.longDescription: Austria's capital and former seat of the Habsburg Empire, with palaces such as Schönbrunn and the Hofburg. The city where Mozart, Beethoven and Strauss lived and worked, it hosts the State Opera and concerts all year, and its traditional coffee houses, recognized by UNESCO as intangible heritage, serve Sachertorte and strudel.

athens.name: Athens
athens.description: The Parthenon atop the Acropolis, historic lanes and tavernas in one of the world's oldest cities.
athens.longDescription: Greece's capital and the cradle of democracy, with the Parthenon crowning the UNESCO-listed Acropolis. From the Acropolis Museum to the Plaka district, the city mixes antiquity and modern life, and tavernas serve souvlaki, feta salads and olives. The Aegean coast is less than an hour away.
athens.imageAlt: The Parthenon on the Acropolis of Athens

zurich.name: Zurich
zurich.description: A clear lake, the Limmat River, a medieval Old Town and the Alps on the horizon.
zurich.longDescription: Switzerland's largest city, on Lake Zurich and cut by the Limmat River, has an Old Town of medieval lanes dominated by the towers of the Grossmünster. In summer you can swim in the river and the lake, and on clear days the Alps appear in the distance. Chocolate and fondue round out the experience.
zurich.imageAlt: The Limmat River and the Grossmünster in Zurich

edinburgh.name: Edinburgh
edinburgh.description: A castle on a volcanic rock, medieval lanes and festivals that fill the city every summer.
edinburgh.longDescription: Scotland's capital, where Edinburgh Castle sits atop an ancient volcanic rock and the Royal Mile runs down to the Palace of Holyroodhouse. The UNESCO-listed Old and New Towns contrast with each other, and Arthur's Seat offers a hike with panoramic views. In August the Edinburgh Festival Fringe takes over the streets.

sydney.name: Sydney
sydney.description: The Opera House, the Harbour Bridge, urban beaches and a harbor that defines the city.
sydney.longDescription: Australia's largest city, built around one of the world's great natural harbors. The UNESCO-listed Opera House and the Harbour Bridge frame the bay, and a short ferry or train ride reaches beaches such as Bondi and Manly. The coastal walk from Bondi to Coogee is one of the most popular outings.
sydney.imageAlt: The Sydney Opera House and Harbour Bridge

melbourne.name: Melbourne
melbourne.description: Street cafés, laneway street art, sport and a cultural scene that never stops.
melbourne.longDescription: The capital of Victoria, known for its café culture and laneways covered in street art, such as Hosier Lane. Federation Square, museums and the Melbourne Cricket Ground sit near the Yarra River, and the city hosts the Australian Open tennis tournament and the Formula 1 Grand Prix.
melbourne.imageAlt: The Melbourne skyline and the Yarra River

auckland.name: Auckland
auckland.description: The City of Sails, with two harbors, dormant volcanoes and islands a short ferry ride away.
auckland.longDescription: New Zealand's largest city, between the Waitematā and Manukau harbours and known as the City of Sails. Built on a volcanic field, it has cones such as Mount Eden overlooking the Sky Tower, and islands such as Waiheke, with vineyards and beaches, about 40 minutes away by ferry.
auckland.imageAlt: The Auckland skyline with the Sky Tower
